title: Blood Pressure Goal in Preterm Preeclampsia
official: Blood Pressure Goal in Preterm Preeclampsia (BLiPP)
summary: The purpose of this study is to compare latency (prolongation of pregnancy from diagnosis till delivery) in patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) with severe features \< 34 weeks gestational age (GA), undergoing expectant management between tight and permissive blood pressure (BP) groups.

interventions.name: Treating BP acutely with intravenous or rapid acting oral medications

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Pregnant individuals
* Age ≥ 18 years old
* HDP with severe features
* Planned inpatient admission for expectant management until delivery
* GA 24 - ≤ 32 weeks GA
* Singleton, non-anomalous fetus
* Anticipated delivery at the study institution

Exclusion criteria:

* HDP with severe features \> 32 weeks gestation at the time of admission
* Poorly controlled preexisting chronic hypertension on ≥2 oral antihypertensive medications
* Preexisting CKD with serum creatinine \> 1.0
* Contraindications to expectant management of preeclampsia with severe features per ACOG (attached)
* Severe FGR (EFW \< 3rd percentile) or FGR with umbilical artery doppler abnormalities (absent or reversed end diastolic flow) at the time of enrollment
* Multiple gestation
* Major fetal anomaly (attached)
* PPROM/active preterm labor
